images.title: Ocean-separated worlds
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: A beautiful high-altitude straight-down world atlas showing SEVEN LARGE ARCHIPELAGOS across an immense ocean. Each archipelago is a cluster of several substantial islands, not a tiny landmark platform. Wide ocean crossings and empty sea must occupy about half the image; no land bridges. Coastlines have complex estuaries, mountains, rivers, settlements, tiny urban footprints and farm plains. No individually huge buildings or ships. The view should feel like Google Maps terrain at global scale on an invented world.
Arrange the seven island groups naturally across the canvas: "Boreal Chain" northwest (snowy mountains, forests, fjords), "Verdant Isles" west-center (fertile green agricultural river deltas), "Ember Arc" southwest (volcanic islands), "Java Commons" east-center (largest populated archipelago with inland plains and eastern coast pin "Port of Beans"), "Monsoon Reach" northeast (lush mountains and island estuaries), "Dune Shelf" southeast (arid islands with desert interiors), "Pelagic Ring" center ocean (dispersed small inhabited islands and reef chains). Emphasize credible large geographic distances; leave ocean routes room to cross.
Subtle map overlays: solid thin blue "Shipping" routes, dashed teal "Data cable" routes and dotted gray "Air" arcs, with a compact legend. A single dashed cable between the western islands and Java has a small broken segment and label "Cable unavailable"; other routes remain visible. No numeric latency claim. Top left search "Search worlds, places, jobs". Upper small layer pills "Terrain / Resources / Transport / Connectivity". Lower left modest selected-region card "Java Commons" and "Explore archipelago". Bottom right scale bar "1,000 km", north arrow and plus/minus. Resources shown only as sparse small pictograms, not lists covering the map. Spacious, large, traversable, coherent.

images.title: Night as operating conditions
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: A detailed high-oblique miniature game view of Port of Beans at blue-hour nightfall, with its lived-in coastal city, ferry harbor, warehouse, modest airport far away, residential blocks and dairy cold store. Streetlights form believable pools of warm light, dark parks and unlit industrial yards remain visible, tiny shift workers and trucks. At one side of the harbor, show a small coastal substation, battery containers, inactive dark solar panels and wind turbines, connected by subtle labeled distribution feeders to cold storage, a hospital block, a water pumping station and a robot charging yard. Physically believable infrastructure, no magical beams.
The player is previewing an overnight electricity allocation. Tiny scene labels "Cold store · Priority", "Water pumps · Priority", "Charging · Deferred". Use a solid teal line for a powered feeder, dashed ochre outline for the deferred charging yard, and one hatched remote district with a question-mark marker "Telemetry stale", distinct from dark-but-powered buildings. Draw no numerical consumption figures.
Minimal UI: top left "Port of Beans / Night operations"; top center "PREVIEW · 21:30 local"; lower left small card "Until dawn" with three short lines "Protect refrigeration", "Reserve water", "Move charging"; bottom right "Review schedule". A very slim night timeline at bottom has "Dusk", "Night shift", "Dawn". Keep the twilight environment dominant and the power system understandable. Night means changing physical needs, not a cosmetic dark-mode filter. No blackout apocalypse, no claim of verified grid safety.

images.title: One shipment across four transport modes
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: An expansive elevated oblique miniature model of a coherent intermodal coastal metro-region, with four distinct transport systems sharing a logistics corridor: cargo airport on a broad inland plateau at upper left (long separated runway and taxiways, modest cargo jets, control tower), freight rail junction and inland yard through middle left, truck interchange and warehouse district center, container harbor and cargo ship at right. Normal city neighborhoods and farmland fill distances between the hubs; all routes fit credible terrain. No giant aircraft, trains on roads, trucks on tracks, or runway through a town. Soft clear late-afternoon light, intricate but legible dollhouse realism.
Follow one shipment with a restrained teal route from a truck at the cold store through the rail yard to the port; a dotted possible air diversion branches toward the cargo terminal. Small labels: "Cold store", "Rail interchange", "Port of Beans", "Air cargo". The selected shipping container has a pin "LOT-204". A small cutaway at the airport operations building reveals a green-screen terminal, subtitled "Legacy dispatch". Do not label all ATC as mainframe.
Minimal HUD: top breadcrumb "Java Commons / Transport / LOT-204". Compact lower-left card "Transfer at rail interchange" with "Custody: Warehouse" and "Rail acceptance: Pending"; bottom-right action "Inspect handoff". Add an inset small route diagram with truck, train, ship and plane icons, the air leg marked "Alternative". Teal is selection, not completed authority. The image should evoke the pleasure of managing a complex transport game where every vehicle and terminal has a job, not a technical dashboard.

images.title: A living food system
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: A richly inhabited isometric miniature farming valley on the Verdant Isles at dawn, surrounded by green hills and a distant ferry harbor. Build a connected working landscape with irregular crop rotation fields, an orchard, a grazing dairy herd and sheltered barn, a poultry enclosure, irrigation reservoir and lined channels, a small feed store, cooperative packhouse and cold room, produce trucks and tiny farm workers. A compact biogas digester beside covered manure storage connects visibly to the farm's utility shed; no sludge pouring into streams. Fallow/cover-crop field and hedgerows show rest and biodiversity, not every inch maximum production. Animals look calm and have space. Rich tactile detail, warm sunrise, playful but credible game scene.
Selective small labels: "North field · Harvest window", "Dairy · Morning care", "Cover crop · Resting", "Cooperative cold store". One small selected cold-chain truck "LOT-204". Top breadcrumb "Verdant Isles / Dawn cooperative". Tiny bottom-left job card "Milk before dawn" with "Animal care / Quality / Delivery". Bottom-right button "Inspect job". A small anchored green-screen cooperative ordering terminal should appear in a glass packhouse office, part of the scenery. No huge metrics, no impossible vertical farm tower, no factory-belt animals, no spectacle. The joy is following food, water, nutrients and work through a lived-in landscape.

images.title: Making parts and building places
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: A beautifully detailed isometric miniature industrial-city district beside Port of Beans, telling a continuous manufacturing-and-construction story. Left side: a modest roof-open factory with raw material racks, machine tools, workbenches, small fenced robot cells, inspection bench, a rework bay and modular wall panels awaiting release. Center: loading dock and short ordinary street with a panel truck. Right side: a school extension construction site, foundation, partly assembled timber/steel structure, tower crane, workers, fenced pedestrian routes, mobile site office and an inspector at a drawing table. Surrounding blocks include finished homes, trees and a tram street. A small materials recycling yard at lower left closes the physical loop. Factories and cranes have sensible proportions; detailed real-material miniature game art, warm daylight.
Use a thin selected teal route following one labeled modular panel batch from inspection bench to truck to site, but put an ochre outlined tag at the inspection bench "Quality hold". Show the panel truck waiting, not implying delivery completed. Exact tiny labels "Factory / Rework / Site / Inspection" near their places.
Top breadcrumb "Port of Beans / Make and build". Bottom-left small order card "School wing / Panel batch P-18", "Design revision C", "Release pending". Bottom-right "Compare build sequence". This is about material provenance, quality, dependencies, crew and time; no magic instantly completed skyscraper, no futuristic nexus, no factory efficiency score.

images.title: A job becomes a better minigame
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: finished visual-styling concept for the proposed Transit World Simulator and Agent OS. Wide landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptional miniature detail and polished editorial map/game art.
Visual language: calm editorial cartography meeting an inhabited simulation game. Small warm-white panels, charcoal typography, sea-glass teal selection, restrained ochre attention. Physical scenery and terrain occupy at least 82% of the image. Thin legible labels. Information comes from labels and line patterns as well as color. No giant HUD dashboards, no neon cyberpunk, no fantasy power core, no performance/success score claims. Exact small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD".
Primary request: A very considered simulation-game scenario comparison screen titled "Milk before dawn". Two synchronized oblique miniature scenes of THE SAME cooperative dairy, farm, cold room, truck yard and rural feeder road, shown side by side at identical camera angle and geometry. Top of left pane "Recorded baseline"; top of right "Candidate". Both show cows calmly sheltered, unchanged buildings, same route to ferry harbor in the distance, same night-to-dawn setting. On left an EV charging row competes visually with cold-store activity and one milk truck waits at a closed dispatch gate. On right the charging row is outlined dashed with label "Charging deferred", cold store has label "Refrigeration reserved", and a proposed truck route is drawn dotted toward the gate. Do not change all equipment into futuristic robots; the modernization is better coordination of the same resources.
A modest dark green legacy terminal inset at lower left pane reads "DISPATCH" and "BATCH WAIT". A small white rule card at lower right pane reads "Proposed schedule" with "Care before collection" and "Check quality before release".
At bottom a slim warm-white shared workbench with four readable steps "Observe → Change rules → Simulate → Review". Under them compact constraint chips "Animal care", "Food quality", "Power reserve", "Delivery window". Bottom-right button "Review changes", alongside "Candidate only · Not applied". No green victory checkmarks or invented pass metrics. Tiny top subtitle "Same weather · Same demand · Same outage". Scenery still dominates, every interface word readable, typography calm and precise. The player can see what the old job feels like and how proposed software coordination could change it without pretending the experiment has already succeeded.
